scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The Gendang Beleq is a traditional dance of the Sasak people of Lombok, West Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia.
It is classified as a sacred folk dance.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed during life-cycle ceremonies such as birth, circumcision, weddings, and funerals.
It is also used for rainfall invocation ceremonies and national holiday celebrations.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a group formation as an orchestra.
Performers march while playing their instruments.
The ensemble is composed of 13 or 17 males, usually young boys.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The ensemble features two large drums (gendang beleq), specifically the male 'gendang mama' and female 'gendang nina'.
Other instruments include the 'Kodeq' drum, a gong, and two reogs (reog nina and reog mama).
Listen for the Gendang mama (male drum), Gendang nina (female drum), Kodeq drum, Gong.
A percussion-heavy ensemble sound led by two large drums that provide dynamic shifts, supported by melodic reogs and a rhythmic gong.
